subject_session: LA11_ses-1 (example) + all 15 sessions / 5 mice (LA11, LA12, LA3, LA8, LA9)
stated_limitation: Two limitations are worth stating. All tones were presented at a single level and at octave spacing, so tuning width is measured coarsely and no rate-level or frequency-response-area analysis is possible. The dandiset provides no electrode table and no unit quality metrics, so every sorted unit is included and tonotopic organisation along the probe cannot be assessed.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000986 is a canonical pure-tone auditory-cortex Neuropixels dataset, exactly the standard choice for demonstrating frequency tuning.
justification.handling: Real NWB files streamed via remfile with correct trial alignment and windows; no unit quality filter is applied, but the dandiset genuinely provides no quality metrics and the run states this explicitly, using statistical responsiveness as the effective selection.
justification.analysis: Methods and statistics are correct and appropriate (Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis, BH-FDR, cross-validated decoder with label-shuffled null, split-half BF reproducibility, and an independent GLM), with circular statistics correctly omitted since frequency is categorical.
justification.correctness: All headline numbers (1564 units, 85% responsive, 645/678 enhanced/suppressed, 598 tuned, median SI 0.68, sparseness 0.68, latency 17 ms, 92% split-half match, 83% decoding) reproduce exactly from the committed CSVs and are internally consistent.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes and show the effect convincingly, including an honestly chosen weakly selective example unit (SI 0.18) alongside sharply tuned ones.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence, the write-up frames the significance tests as a high-powered screen and defers to effect-size measures, and it names concrete limitations of this specific result.
